name: Lomo Saltado (Peruvian Steak Stir-fry)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 3 pounds (900 g) beef tenderloin or other tender steak
4 tomatoes, seeds removed, puréed in a blender
5 potatoes peeled and cut into strips for frying
1 yellow Peruvian Chili Pepper (aji), cut into thin strips

steps: Cut the meat into thin strips and marinate them in the wine for 1 hour.
Use a wok to cook garlic in oil over medium heat and add the meat. Reserve the juice.
Add the tomato purée, salt and pepper. Cook for a few minutes.
Add the soy sauce while stirring the meat in the wok.
Add the onions, aji strips, cilantro and vinegar. Combine the juice from the meat.
Fry the potatoes in a separate pan and add to the other ingredients.
Serve the dish with white rice.

culture.text: Lomo saltado is a traditional Peruvian dish, a stir-fry that typically combines marinated strips of sirloin with onions, tomatoes, french fries, and other ingredients, and is typically served with rice. The dish originated as part of the chifa tradition, the Chinese cuisine of Peru, though its popularity has made it part of the mainstream culture.
